Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

polychoice 0.1.0

Initial CRAN release. Features:

  • Estimators mnl() (multinomial / conditional logit), imnl() (baseline-inflated multinomial logit of Bagozzi and Marchetti 2017; with several inflated alternatives the parametrized logit captivity model of Swait and Ben-Akiva 1987), nlogit() (two-level nested logit), hev() (heteroskedastic extreme value), mnprobit() (multinomial probit), remnl() (random alternative-specific intercepts, adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature), rologit() (rank-ordered logit for complete, partial, and tied rankings, with the exact tie likelihood of Allison and Christakis 1994).
  • Firth’s penalized likelihood for mnl() and rologit() (firth = TRUE): finite estimates under separation, with tied rankings through the information of the exact tie probability; profile penalized-likelihood intervals (confint()) and penalized likelihood-ratio tests (term_test(), combine_test(), lr_test(), rank_test()). The penalized likelihood can have more than one local maximum, so a penalized fit also runs from the maximum-likelihood estimate and keeps the higher.
  • Priors for mnl() and rologit() (prior = coef_prior(...)): normal, Cauchy or t priors centred at zero on coefficients scaled to their columns (Gelman et al. 2008), fitted as the posterior mode, with the same penalized machinery as firth = TRUE; fits under several priors show how much of a separated estimate comes from the prior.
  • separation(): an exact check of separation for mnl() and rologit() data (a linear program on the comparisons the choices or rankings report, ties included, through lpSolveAPI), which their maximum-likelihood fits use to name diverging coefficients. Under separation the maximum-likelihood forms of term_test(), combine_test(), lr_test() and boot_lr_test() compare the suprema of the log-likelihoods, not where the optimizer stopped.
  • boot_lr_test() also calibrates the comparison of two nested rologit() fits, drawing rankings with each case’s observed rank groups.
  • Wide and long data layouts, varying choice sets, frequency weights, offsets, unit fixed effects with the never-chosen rule and the split-panel jackknife (bias_correct = "jackknife"), analytic / outer-product / robust / cluster / bootstrap standard errors.
  • Quantities of interest: predict() (probabilities, classes, utilities, outcome-stage and regime probabilities, posterior regime probabilities), first_difference(), rrr().
  • Fit and comparison: fit_stats(), classification(), lr_test(), vuong(), boot_lr_test(), compare_models(); broom, texreg, and modelsummary support.
  • IIA and specification tests: hausman_mcfadden(), small_hsiao(), fp_tests(), iia_tests(), nested_lm_test(), combine_test(), term_test(), hl_test(), boot_pvalue() (the parametric bootstrap of the tests whose null is the fitted model); rank_test() (stability of preferences across ranking stages); captivity_test() (score test of the multinomial logit against captive choosers, the dogit of Gaudry and Dagenais 1979, and with type = "lr" the likelihood ratio against a constant captive share, which lr_test() also takes).
  • Simulators rmnl(), rnlogit(), rhev(), rmnp(), rrologit(); mundlak().
  • Data sets pa2006 and pres2004 (Bagozzi and Marchetti 2017), and sanctions, fluvax, bes1987, defection, bes2010, cabinets, afghan_leaders from published replication archives, with the vignette Seven published analyses.

Developed by Benjamin E. Bagozzi.
